audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Lillia 4 of 7 stages while the Emerald+ win rate is 33.33%, and the two layers disagree at stage 7 (win[6] Lillia vs phases[6].side Skill).
audit.why: Every why-string on the page already argues the packet chart — whys[0..2] describe Garen winning outright, whys[3..5] describe coin-flips, whys[6] is Lillia's. Only the enum rows and the full-layer why text carried the old optimistic reading. The mirror rewrote the Garen page to the packet chart, so this side must match it.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet: Garen / Garen / Garen / Skill / Skill / Skill / Lillia, in both layers, with ratings and full-layer why text moved with it.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d invents a 'fifteen-second' Courage window and no spike text carries a real number.
audit.why: Courage is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 — 22s at rank 1, not 15. Decisive Strike is 8s flat, Judgment 9s at rank 1, Demacian Justice 120s at rank 1, and Lilting Lullaby costs 150s at rank 1. Those numbers are what make 'commit on its cooldown' actionable.
audit.corrected: Twenty-two-second invitation; Courage 22s and Decisive Strike 8s written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and the spike/why text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in the lane is absent: Decisive Strike purges Swirlseed's slow.
audit.why: Riot's text for Decisive Strike: 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him.' Swirlseed's slow is Lillia's only pin, and it dies to an 8-second cooldown. A player who does not know this throws E at a step-up and then wonders why the kite failed. The mirror recorded the same interaction from Garen's side.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[0], whys[2], wants.you[2], early, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Courage's tenacity is mentioned only as a vague 'tenacity so your E-slow and R-sleep barely hold him'.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Courage a shield AND tenacity for a brief moment, then lesser damage reduction for longer. Tenacity shortens the Drowsy window on a 150-second ultimate, which is the concrete reason to bait it first.
audit.corrected: Courage named with 22s and all three components; Drowsy called out by name.

audit.why: Demacian Justice is correctly described as missing-HP TRUE damage — Riot's flags confirm trueDamage and execute, so no amount of MR saves a low Lillia. Blooming Blows' outer ring is likewise true damage, which is why her chip still lands into his stacked resists from Courage's passive.
audit.corrected: True-damage edge added to breakdown.cooldowns; execute text left intact.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet defect: the page never named Perseverance, Decisive Strike, Judgment or Demacian Justice anywhere in the content layer.
audit.why: Generic 'his Q', 'his spin', 'his passive regen' is exactly the vagueness the rewrite bar exists to kill.
audit.corrected: All four named in the content layer at their real slots.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swirlseed's terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact.
audit.why: Riot's description says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target — it does not create terrain. The mirror reached the same conclusion.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Garen and you have to respect it. His Q silences your W mid-wind-up and lands an empowered strike, so if you step in to land a Q sweetspot you eat a silence-and-spin trade you can't kite out of yet. You only have one ability at level 1 and no movement-speed chain, so farm with the very tip of your Q from max range and do not throw E into his spin range hoping for a slow — he'll just Q-silence and walk you down. His passive regen heals the little Dream Dust chip you do land, so early ticks barely matter.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Garen and you have to respect it. Decisive Strike silences your Watchful Wisp mid-wind-up and lands an empowered strike, so stepping in for a Q sweetspot buys a silence-and-Judgment trade you cannot kite out of yet. With one ability at level 1 and no move-speed chain, farm with the very tip of your Q and do not throw Swirlseed hoping for a slow — his Q breaks free of all slows on an 8-second cooldown and he simply walks you down. Perseverance regenerates the little Dream Dust chip you land, so early ticks barely matter.
